summary: kepler resolves dependency from non-registry host with install scripts enabled
details: package.json declares the dependency `flag-serial-object-syntax` with a direct URL resolution to `https://artifacts.yosiroute.com/npm/flag-serial-object-syntax` rather than the npm registry, and npm-shrinkwrap.json records `hasInstallScript: true` for that dependency. Running `npm install kepler` fetches a tarball from artifacts.yosiroute.com and executes its lifecycle scripts on the installer's machine, resolving code from a third-party host outside the npm registry's distribution channel. Package metadata is placeholder (author `Package Registry`, description `Generated package`, repository `github.com/example/kepler`) and the version is `5.0.999`, a pattern consistent with a dependency-confusion lure intended to be resolved in preference to a private internal `kepler` package.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
